newsitem.title: USA: EPA proposing rule to close offshore NJ dump site.
newsitem.headline: EPA proposing rule to close offshore NJ dump site.

text.p: The Environmental Protection Agency will propose a rule next week to close a controversial offshore New Jersey ocean dumping site by September 1, EPA Administrator Carol Browner announced on Wednesday.

"(This action) is good for the environment and good for the economy," Browner said at a press briefing called to outline the latest development in EPA's plan to close Mud Dump Site, the nation's last ocean dumping site.

EPA and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers kicked off the initiative last year by announcing an agreement to expedite dredging the Port of New Jersey and New York to make it viable for future use by the time the dump site is closed this fall.
Browner said the proposed rule and a supplemental environmental impact statement for closing the site will appear in the Federal Register on May 16.

She said the Corps and EPA are "expediting" 10 "high priority" permit applications for Federal Maintenance Dredging Projects, in addition to several applications from private parties that want to use Mud Dump Site for disposal before it closes.

"Today's announcement ensures that we're on schedule to enact a permanent and long overdue ban on the destructive practice of ocean dumping," U.S. Sen. Robert Torricelli, a Democrat from New Jersey, said in a press statement.
"It's a huge step forward for the protection of our oceanfronts and for the quality of life of all of us in New Jersey."
